subject: Pricing: graduated commit ladder + spot-burst opt-in
messages:
From: Ava Schultz <ava@logitechia.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: looking for pricing for variable burst usage

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick summary of our ask: we run a base load for our conversational agent (~300M tokens/month) but have frequent, predictable spikes tied to marketing pushes and product launches where we hit 1.0–1.5B tokens/day for 48–72 hour windows.

Two specific questions:
- Can you describe how Redwood handles on-demand over commit? Is there a clear per-token overage rate for short bursts?
- Do you offer a lower-priced "spot burst" option if we accept preemption or rate-limiting during extreme events? If so, how does billing and SLA work?

Our procurement team will need minimum spend language and an invoice-friendly breakdown by line item. I attached a short Q2 forecast so you can see the cadence.

Attachment: LogiTechia_Q2_forecast.pdf (2 pages)

Would love to get a proposal / sample pricing ladder we could review. Happy to set a follow-up call.

Best,
Ava Schultz
Head of Product, LogiTechia
ava@logitechia.com

From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Schultz <ava@logitechia.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial: looking for pricing for variable burst usage

Hi Ava — appreciated the forecast, this is a familiar pattern for many of our customers. High-level proposal below, I can put formal numbers into a pricing table and SOW after we sync on the structure:

1) Graduated Commit Ladder (monthly, per-token pricing):
- Tier A: 250–500M tokens/month — standard commit rate (X per 1M tokens)
- Tier B: 500–1B tokens/month — reduced commit rate (X-15% per 1M)
- Tier C: 1B+ tokens/month — best-in-class commit rate (X-25% per 1M)

2) On-demand over-commit (burst) behavior:
- When usage exceeds committed tokens in a month, on-demand rate applies for excess tokens charged per 1M tokens.
- For short high-frequency spikes (under 72 hours), we can structure an "on-demand smoothing" true-up so you aren't immediately penalized for a single campaign spike; true-up cadence visible in the billing console.

3) Spot-burst opt-in (lower-cost burst capacity with preemption):
- Customers can opt into a spot-burst pool at a significantly lower rate for excess tokens. In exchange, requests served from the spot pool may be preempted or queued during capacity contention.
- We propose a parity metric: if more than Y% of spot requests are preempted for >Z seconds during a campaign window, Redwood issues a partial credit to affected burst spend (we can define the %/seconds).

4) Minimum spend and contract mechanics:
- We recommend a minimum monthly commit floor (e.g., 250M) to qualify for tiered pricing.
- Overage is billed monthly; true-up and credits are performed on the same cadence.

If this structure sounds reasonable I'll draft a pricing table with concrete per-1M-token numbers and a pilot SOW. Would you be open to a 30-minute call this week?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Schultz <ava@logitechia.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-14T08:31:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial: looking for pricing for variable burst usage

Looping in commercial — can approve a pilot concession with these guardrails:
- 10% off the committed per-token rate at the 750M tier for a three-month pilot.
- Offer spot-burst pricing at 40% of standard on-demand burst rate for the pilot (limited to X TB of spot capacity per month).
- Pilot SOW will include preemption credit language: if >15% of requests routed to spot are preempted for >30s during a single campaign day, credit = 15% of that day's spot spend.

Please attach the pilot SOW draft and the preliminary pricing table. Finance needs line-item structure for invoicing.

Attachment: pilot_sow_draft.docx (placeholder)

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Ava Schultz <ava@logitechia.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@logitechia.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial: looking for pricing for variable burst usage

Thanks Rafael and Marissa — the structure looks promising. A few follow-ups from our side before legal/procurement will sign off:
- Can you clarify the SLA/notification process for spot preemption? We need advance notice when possible and a post-mortem if preemption impacts a campaign.
- The proposed credit formula is okay, but we need a cap (e.g., credit cannot exceed Y% of monthly spend) and clarity on how credits are applied (invoice credit vs. cash).
- Procurement asks for a monthly true-up and a sample invoice showing line items: committed tokens, on-demand overage, spot-burst usage, credits.
- Also, is there an option to commit to a small buffer of reserved burst capacity (short-term add-on) to avoid preemption for mission-critical launches? If yes, how is that priced?

Looping in Luis (procurement) to track the SOW and invoice format.

Best,
Ava

Luis Ortega
Procurement Manager, LogiTechia
luis.ortega@logitechia.com

From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Schultz <ava@logitechia.com>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@logitechia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-18T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial: looking for pricing for variable burst usage

Thanks — great questions, Luis. Proposed answers and next steps below. I've attached a concise pricing table with concrete numbers for review.

1) SLA/notification for spot preemption:
- We will provide best-effort advance notifications when spot pool eviction is expected (when system signals sustained >85% utilization). For incidents that occur without advance notice we will publish post-incident reports for any event that causes >10% request impact for >1 hour.

2) Credit mechanics:
- Credit = 10% of affected spot spend for qualifying preemption events (this is applied as an invoice credit the following month). Credits capped at 25% of monthly committed spend for the pilot period.

3) True-up and invoice format:
- Monthly true-up cadence; invoice will show: committed tokens (line A), on-demand overage (line B), spot-burst usage (line C), credits (line D) with a final total. We'll provide a sample invoice PDF for procurement.

4) Reserved short-term burst add-on:
- We can offer a "burst-reserve" add-on (N tokens reserved for up to 7 days) priced at a modest premium to spot but below full on-demand. This is billed pro-rata for the reservation window and intended for mission-critical launches.

Consolidated proposal for pilot (numbers example):
- Monthly commit: 750M tokens at commit rate $X per 1M (10% pilot discount applied)
- On-demand overage: $Y per 1M tokens
- Spot-burst pilot rate: $0.40 * Y per 1M
- Burst-reserve: $0.65 * Y per 1M reserved (pro-rata for reservation days)
- Credit: 10% of affected spot spend, capped at 25% of monthly committed spend

Next steps: I attached final_pricing_table.csv and a link to a short SOW draft in Drive. If this looks acceptable I'll loop legal to convert the pilot SOW into an executable addendum and get you a sample invoice for procurement. Can we target a pilot kickoff the week of 2027-06-07?

Attachments: final_pricing_table.csv (CSV)
Related links: https://drive.redwood/proposals/LDG-2027-05-001

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
